subject: Can I pass the gradient to Stan too?

messages.author: 40b63348dbcb447d
messages.subject: Can I pass the gradient to Stan too?
parts:
Hi, my log posterior is quite complex and I am not sure Stan can efficiently compute it. So I have already calculated it by hand, can I somehow pass it to Stan? Thanks.

Best,
Ziyuan

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Can I pass the gradient to Stan too?
parts:
On Sunday, February 24, 2013 7:09:55 AM UTC-5, ZiYuan Lin wrote:
Hi, my log posterior is quite complex and I am not sure Stan can efficiently compute it. So I have already calculated it by hand, can I somehow pass it to Stan?

No. With some effort, you could customize the generated C++ file to use an analytic gradient. Or Radford Neal's GRIMS package can do HMC in R with a function that computes the gradient analytically. 

However, the auto-differentiation mechanism in Stan is pretty clever and only contributes a constant multiple to the complexity of evaluating the log-posterior.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can I pass the gradient to Stan too?
parts:
What is it? Stan's auto-diff's pretty efficient for
everything for which there are analytic gradients.
And it uses dynamic programming on the expression graph
for shared subexpessions.

Of course, you can still do better by hand.

One problem with supplying gradients is that they need to
be on the unconstrained scale and need to take into account
any log Jacobian determinant adjustments entailed by the
constraints on parameters.

- Bob

messages.author: 1004dd6f66bb10c3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Can I pass the gradient to Stan too?
parts:
The answer is yes, but it's a pain. You'll have to override
grad_log_prob() in the c++ code that Stan generates to implement your
model, which requires a certain amount of familiarity with how Stan is
implemented.

Matt
